Article Title: UN approves resolution to declare Nov 27 as ‘International Day For Elimination Of Child, Early & Forced Marriage’
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a significant development that brings focus on the need to step up action to deliver on the Sustainable Development Goals 2030, the United Nations (UN) has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone, as it was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign in 2024.Even though underage marriage has been declining over the decades, the numbers are still a concern calling for greater efforts to eradicate the problem. According to the 2019-21 National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 23.3% of women aged 20-24 were married before the age of 18. This came down to 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Just Rights for Children founder Bhuwan Ribhu, who has been vociferously advocating for a dedicated day and has worked closely with the drafting of the resolution, said that the announcement is very significant for India as it is an opportunity to lead by example and meet the elimination targets.Welcoming the UN approval for the demand from countries across the world, Ribhu said, “Today marks the tipping point, showing that the end of the crime of child marriage is inevitable and imminent.Now is the time for governments globally to provide decisive leadership to end child marriage by 2030 and ensure education, protection and development of every child to realise their full potential. I am grateful to the First Lady of Sierra Leone for her leadership in championing this cause and would also like to thank the countries that co-sponsored our resolution. “ He was present at the UN as the civil society representative when the UN approved the resolution.“The Government of India has set a target of reducing the prevalence of child marriage by 10% by 2026. With continued efforts at the national and state levels, the prevalence of child marriage in India is expected to fall below 15% by the end of 2026. The global commitment to eliminate child marriage by 2030 is aligned with target 5.3 of Sustainable Development Goal 5 (Gender Equality), which calls for the elimination of all harmful practices, including child, early, and forced marriage,” Ribhu added.He shared that plans are afoot to hold extensive outreach campaigns in coordination with the govt and states ahead of November 27 to ensure that the day becomes a space to dwell on progress made and the way forward and does not end up as a symbolic reminder of the problem.
Article Summary: The UN has declared November 27 the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage. The date carries special significance for India, which backed the resolution steered by Sierra Leone. It was on Nov 27 that the govt had launched the ‘Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat’ campaign.

Article Title: ‘Will be compelled to launch large-scale agitation’: Sonam Wangchuk ahead of Ladakh talks with Centre
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands.“If stepmotherly treatment is meted out to Ladakh and the people living along the borders, then we will be compelled to launch a very large-scale agitation after September 9,” PTI quoted him as saying. He was referring to the date when an LAB sub-committee is scheduled to meet Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) officials in Delhi to press for its demands.Wangchuk further announced that the outfit's proposed march from Kargil to Leh, scheduled to begin on September 10, had been postponed in view of the MHA talks. However, he warned the march would be revived if the talks fail to produce a “satisfactory” outcome.“We have collectively decided to postpone the 'padyatra' for the time being. We will once again appeal to people from across India to come forward in support of Ladakh, in support of the environment, and in support of the people of Ladakh who remain steadfast on the country's borders,” he stated.He added that the LAB is observing September as “Martyrs' Month” in memory of those killed, injured and jailed last year.The activist was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year, during which four civilians were killed, allegedly in police firing. Wangchuk himself was detained under the stringent National Security Act and released six months later, in March this year.Wangchuk, who emerged as the face of the recent student protests in Delhi and sat on a hunger strike for more than 20 days, also said the LAB expects the Centre to bring a detailed draft on the proposed Ladakh assembly, including its powers and rights, to the September 9 meeting.The outfit has been demanding legislation for Ladakh at the Union territory level, safeguards under Article 371, withdrawal of cases filed after the September 24 violence last year, compensation for victims and publication of the inquiry commission report. The LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) have been jointly spearheading the agitation since Ladakh was granted Union territory status in August 2019 and have held several rounds of talks with the Centre since 2021.
Article Summary: Ladakh-based activist Sonam Wangchuk said the Leh Apex Body (LAB) would be compelled to launch a “very large-scale agitation” if the Union government fails to make “concrete” progress on the group’s key demands. He was referring to the violence in Leh, the Union territory's capital, on September 24 last year.

Article Title: Ganga rises above 'highest flood mark' in Patna; several low-lying areas face inundation risk

NEW DELHI: The Ganga breached the ‘highest flood mark’ at Patna’s Gandhi Ghat amid heavy rain in Bihar, with the river’s water level rising 10 cm in four hours on Saturday morning, according to an official bulletin.The river was flowing 1 cm above the highest flood level at 10 am, reaching 50.53 metres at Gandhi Ghat, the Water Resources Department (WRD) said.“The Ganga water level at Gandhi Ghat in Patna rose by 10 cm in the past four hours, reaching 50.53 cm, which is 1 cm above the highest flood level, at 10 am on Saturday,” the department said in its latest bulletin, as quoted by PTI.The situation could worsen further, with the WRD forecasting a continued rise in the river’s water level. “The forecast is that the Ganga water level at Gandhi Ghat is likely to rise further to 50.62 cm by 8 am on Sunday. People have been advised to exercise caution,” it said.The rising water has raised concerns over possible inundation in low-lying areas of Patna, with people being urged to remain cautious.Several districts across Bihar are already facing flood-like conditions as heavy rainfall in the state and neighbouring Nepal has pushed multiple rivers above their danger marks.The Ganga, Gandak, Kosi, Burhi Gandak, Bagmati, Punpun and Ghaghra are among the rivers flowing above danger levels.Chief minister Samrat Choudhary conducted an aerial survey of the affected areas on Friday and reviewed relief and rescue operations.He directed officials to identify affected families and ensure they receive relief on time. He also ordered continuous monitoring of vulnerable areas and the Ganga embankments between Buxar and Bhagalpur to prevent erosion and possible breaches.
Article Summary: The Ganga breached the ‘highest flood mark’ at Patna’s Gandhi Ghat amid heavy rain in Bihar. The river was flowing 1 cm above the highest flood level at 10 am, reaching 50.53 metres. The rising water has raised concerns over possible inundation in low-lying areas of Patna.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the NEET agitation at Jantar Mantar and said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing.While speaking at the launch of former secretary (security) Yashovardhan Azad's book "Policing the Republic", Justice Bhuyan said that police must maintain their credibility because people seek their help when they feel wronged."All of us are dismayed when we see young officers of the Indian Police Service personally going and assaulting protesters and demonstrators. This is something very, very distressing to observe. The detachment expected of police officers somehow seems to be disappearing, and this is indeed a matter of grave concern," Justice Bhuyan said."For most common people, a policeman on the street wearing a whistle and a lathi represents the power and authority of the state. When they feel wronged, they seek the help of the police. It is, therefore, of utmost importance that the police force maintains its credibility.It can do so only by strictly adhering to the Constitution, by functioning as a truly professional force, acting impartially, displaying courage and acting with conviction, maintaining integrity and adhering to secular principles, thereby upholding the rule of law," he said.The Supreme Court judge further said that if government functionaries become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and encourage lawlessness."If the functionaries of the government become lawbreakers, it is bound to breed contempt for the law and will encourage lawlessness. No civilised nation can permit that to happen. Does a citizen shed his fundamental right the moment a policeman arrests him?" Justice Bhuyan said.The alleged use of force by Delhi Police during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and the march towards Parliament has come under the Supreme Court's scrutiny, with the court constituting a high-level panel to examine complaints of excessive force.The panel, headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice R Subhash Reddy, will investigate allegations against Delhi Police and examine evidence including CCTV footage and videos of the protests.Among the allegations to be examined are the use of lathis, tear gas, pellet guns and electronic batons, as well as claims of targeted harassment and molestation of women protesters.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticised police officers over the alleged assault on protesting students during the NEET agitation. He said that the detachment expected of officials appears to be disappearing. The alleged use of force by Delhi Police during the July 20 student protests at Jantar Mantar and the march towards Parliament has come under scrutiny.

Article Title: 'Step beyond books to connect with children': PM Modi's message on Teachers' Day

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged teachers to “step beyond textbooks” to ensure that children do not lose out on their childhood.The prime minister's message came during his interaction with recipients of the National Teachers’ Awards at his residence on Friday, a day ahead of Teachers’ Day, which commemorates the birth anniversary of former President and renowned educationist Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan."We need to step outside of books and the syllabus much more than before and get into the lives of children. Childhood shouldn't be allowed to die. And the biggest task of keeping childhood alive can be done by a teacher. It's the teacher's job to ensure the child within remains," he said.To drive home his point, PM Modi cited growing screen addiction among children, particularly their increasing dependence on video games. He also flagged drug consumption as a concern, saying the problem was no longer confined to universities or major cities."Screen time has now become a form of addiction. A thought occurs to me: if a child begins to take a keen interest in sports, and by sports, I don't mean video games but actually playing on the field. Then slowly, they can come out of it. And we should make it a habit to involve kids as much as possible in creativity, and we should design some programmes for that," the prime minister said."Now take the case of drugs. It's not just in big cities or universities anymore, nobody even knows what it is; someone just comes and gives it. Teachers should watch for behavioural changes in children," he added.Saturday marks the 138th birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who also served as Vice President of India. Later in the day, PM Modi will visit Shri Ram College of Commerce, which is celebrating its centenary.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi urges teachers to ensure children do not lose out on their childhood. He cites growing screen addiction among children, particularly their dependence on video games. Saturday marks the 138th birth anniversary of Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, who served as Vice President of India.

Article Title: 'Exceptionally rare': All 3 hydraulic systems of Air India Phuket-Delhi flight failed together
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

‘Triple hydraulic failure close to unthinkable’

MUMBAI: Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report has confirmed what pilots and engineers call an exceptionally rare event, the near-simultaneous loss of all three hydraulic systems on the A320neo aircraft at 36,000 feet. Hydraulic systems are the fluid-pressure circuits that physically move an aircraft's wing and tail surfaces. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset that injured 24 flyers.The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb from 34,000 feet to 36,000 feet after entering the airspace controlled by Kolkata ATC. At 9:32:43am IST, within four seconds the flight control system detected loss of all the three hydraulic systems.In the next few seconds, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. “The aircraft encountered altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 ft and fell by 292 ft from its assigned 36,000 feet flight level during the event,” the report said.It did not give information on the cause of the triple hydraulic failure, nor did it put forth any safety recommendations for the A320 aircraft type. It said the investigation is in progress and hydraulic components, fluid samples and recorder data have been collected and are still being analysed.The critical information on the probable cause and contributory factors is likely to be released in the final report, expected to be published on or before Aug 4, 2027.In simple terms, hydraulic pressure is what physically moves an aircraft’s control surfaces, the ailerons on the wings that make it roll, the elevators on the tail that make it pitch up or down, and the rudder that makes it yaw left or right. Pilots move the stick and pedals, but it is hydraulic power that pushes the actual surfaces. An A320 carries three independent hydraulic circuits so that losing one, or even two, still leaves enough pressure to fly and manoeuvre the aircraft normally.“Losing all three at once is considered close to unthinkable, because the A320 has a triple-redundant hydraulic design which ensures no combination of failures can disable flight controls entirely. It is the kind of failure engineers cite alongside a handful of decades-old incidents involving other aircraft types, none of them an A320,” said a senior aircraft maintenance engineer. The notable total hydraulic loss events that occurred globally are the 1985 JAL 123 (Boeing 747), the 1989 United Airlines DC-10, and a DHL A300 that was hit by a missile over Baghdad in 2003.Following the triple hydraulic failure, the co-pilot, who was flying the aircraft, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift, the blue system came back within seconds, followed shortly by yellow and green, restoring normal flight control surfaces, the report said.
Article Summary: The accident occurred when the eight-year-old A320neo (VT-EXO) carrying 145 people had just been cleared to climb to 36,000 feet. The green, blue and yellow systems dropped out within seconds of each other, triggering an autopilot disengagement, a stall warning and a brief altitude upset.

Article Title: Coal stock at thermal plants plummets, 'critical' at 50 units
Article Text:

Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel

NEW DELHI: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level, with 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2 amid high electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies, Central Electricity Authority data showed.The plants, with a combined capacity of around 224 GW, had 28.2 million tonnes (MT) of coal as of Wednesday, 48% of the prescribed requirement of 58.7 MT. The available stock is equivalent to about nine days of coal requirement at 85% plant load factor, against the normal requirement of around 19 days.The plants classified as short on coal stocks have less than 25% of their normative inventories. Coal ministry officials, however, said all critical plants were being monitored by an inter-ministerial team of officials on a day-to-day basis and regular fuel supplies were being provided to them.Of the 50 plants, 45 are based on domestic fuel, four are designed for imported coal and one runs on washery rejects.A senior coal ministry official said, "Classification of a thermal power plant as critical is a routine monitoring parameter under norms laid down by CEA. It simply means closer tracking and priority action. These plants are not running out of supply."Though the normative coal requirement at power plants is calculated at 3.1 MT every day at 85% plant load factor, officials said the actual requirement is around 2.4 MT.The monsoon sees supply disruptions every year. The situation starts improving from Sept onwards as rains begin to recede.While the power ministry did not respond to requests for a reaction, sources said some coal-fired plants had been asked to defer scheduled maintenance to ensure continuity of electricity generation.
Article Summary: Coal stocks at thermal power plants across the country have fallen to less than half the recommended level. 50 plants classified as having 'critically low' inventories as on Sept 2. High electricity demand and monsoon-led disruptions in supplies blamed.

Article Title: Europe waking up to Modi's warning 'a bit late': Belgian PM
Article Text:

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever on Friday said Europe had been slow to recognise the risks of becoming too dependent on other economies, admitting that Indian PM Narendra Modi had warned it about the problem much earlier but was not heard.De Wever, who was on a two-day visit to India to strengthen ties in trade, investment, technology and strategic cooperation, said India and Europe were now facing similar challenges as economic dependencies were increasingly being used as leverage. "We do not like dependencies becoming weaponised against us. You have lived this history. Your Prime Minister warned Europe about this long time ago already. But he was ignored. He wasn't listened to. We are listening now," De Wever said at a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) event.Calling Europe's awakening "a bit late", De Wever said the region was now having the "right debates" about who it could work with in a world where major economic powers were moving in different directions.He said India was the most important partner for Europe among countries that believed in multilateralism and cooperation based on "respect and not force"."If India is not on the list, then you have missed something fundamental. India is on that list. It's number one," De Wever said.In an apparent reference to China, De Wever said Europe was seeking to reduce its dependence on "big economical powerhouses" that were moving away from rules-based cooperation. "I will not name them China," he said, adding that such a direction was not what Europe wanted.Speaking on the occasion, Union commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the India-EU FTA was a win-win for everyone. "It will open opportunities for farmers, start ups, women entrepreneurs, it has something for everyone. It's been deftly negotiated protecting sensitive sectors on both sides. It offers huge potential for both sides," he said.

NEW DELHI: Jalandhar Commissionerate Police detained Manjit Singh Bedi, a fugitive wanted in the US in connection with an alleged SNAP benefits fraud case, Punjab Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav said on Friday.Bedi was reportedly placed on the US Most-Wanted Fraudsters list over allegations of defrauding the US government of more than $600,000 through a scheme involving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. According to the Punjab DGP, Bedi allegedly fled to India via Canada in April 2026 to evade US law enforcement."In a major breakthrough, Jalandhar Commissionerate Police apprehends Manjit Singh Bedi, a wanted fugitive linked to a US-based benefits fraud case. Bedi was reportedly placed on the US Most-Wanted Fraudsters list in connection with a SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits fraud case in the #USA and had allegedly fled to #India via #Canada in April 2026 to evade the law," the DGP posted on X.The FBI had earlier alleged that Bedi, an India-born naturalised US citizen, operated Asian Grocery Store in Tacoma, Washington, where he used customers' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards to process transactions without providing food.He allegedly gave SNAP participants cash instead and kept half of the proceeds.“Instead of selling participants food, Bedi is alleged to have swiped their cards and given them cash,” the FBI said in its wanted notice.Bedi was indicted in the US on charges of wire fraud and SNAP benefits fraud. He was initially allowed to appear in court without being arrested and was ordered to surrender his passport and remain in Washington state, but the FBI said he later fled to Canada and then India.A federal arrest warrant was issued against him on May 21, 2026, in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington after he allegedly violated the conditions of his supervision. The FBI had offered a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.The Punjab DGP said the police force remains committed to tracking fugitives and tackling transnational organised crime.“Punjab Police remains relentless in tracking down fugitives and dismantling transnational organised crime networks, ensuring that no one can evade justice by crossing borders,” he said.In a separate development earlier on Friday, the State Special Operation Cell (SSOC) Amritsar and Counter Intelligence Amritsar arrested six people in two operations targeting alleged weapons and narcotics smuggling modules.Police recovered 2.9 kg of heroin, eight high-end pistols and six live cartridges, besides impounding a car and a motorcycle allegedly used in the smuggling activities.Preliminary investigation indicated that the accused were allegedly involved in cross-border smuggling and received weapons and narcotics consignments through drones for distribution among criminal elements in Punjab, the DGP said. Further investigation is underway to establish the network's forward and backward linkages.
Article Summary: Jalandhar Commissionerate Police detained Manjit Singh Bedi, a fugitive wanted in the US in connection with an alleged SNAP benefits fraud case. According to the Punjab DGP, Bedi allegedly fled to India via Canada in April 2026.

Article Title: SC awards pension to Mumbai engineer who forged ST certificate
Article Text:
SC allowed him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court has rewarded a wrongdoer - a man who got appointed as a junior civil engineer in Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) by producing a forged ST certificate, and, subsequently, stalled the scrutiny of his eligibility for quota for more than a decade - by allowing him to superannuate in peace with retirement benefits.Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. He misplaced the original ST certificate but managed to secure a fresh one from the sub-divisional magistrate, Bhusawal division, in Oct 2000.Following scrutiny initiated by MCGM, the Police Vigilance Cell traced Patil's family history and found that his ancestors had been recorded as 'Koli', 'Hindu Koli' and 'Hindu Suryawanshi Koli', none of which belonged to the ST category. In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil.He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee until Jan 2020, when the panel rejected his plea that his lawyer and elderly family members were not available, and invalidated the ST certificate. HC dismissed his appeal against cancellation of ST status.SC, however, stayed Patil's dismissal from service through an interim order on Nov 18, 2021.As a result, the engineer continued to serve until June 30, 2025, when he retired after being employed with MCGM for more than three decades based on a forged ST certificate.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi Thursday upheld the cancellation of Patil's ST certificate and Bombay HC order. However, it took a lenient view given his undertaking that he or any of his family members "shall (not) be entitled to claim any future benefit on the basis of the invalidated ST certificate".The ruling contrasts with SC's consistent rulings against benefits accruing to people who forge SC or ST certificates to gain admission or employment.
Article Summary: Shirish P Patil got a certificate in 1984 by identifying himself as belonging to the 'Tokre Koli' Scheduled Tribe community. Based on the certificate, he was appointed a junior civil engineer in MCGM in 1994. In July 2009, MCGM issued a show cause notice to Patil. He successfully dodged and delayed proceedings before the scrutiny committee.

Article Title: 'Cracked skull' wasn't all: In eye of storm, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj
Article Text:
Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district.

A provocative online presence

The hunt for Bhardwaj

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: Long before the viral video in which he boasted about assaulting a Jantar Mantar protester’s father, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj had built a sizeable following through provocative posts, political associations and incendiary remarks.Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday, hours after Delhi Police assured protesters from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that he would be arrested within 72 hours.Bhardwaj is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20.His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which Bhardwaj is heard claiming that he had "cracked the skull" of the father."Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didn't get justice."But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was out and about through the night," Bhardwaj is heard saying in the video.He then named several political leaders while explaining why, according to him, he had little reason to fear arrest."I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he claimed.There is, however, no evidence to establish that any of the political leaders named by Bhardwaj intervened on his behalf in the case.The viral clip also brought renewed attention to Bhardwaj's older social media posts and videos.According to news agency PTI, his Facebook page, which has around 327,000 followers, contains posts focused on cow protection, attacks on Muslims and critics of the government, as well as photographs appearing to show his proximity to political figures and official events.Some older videos circulating on social media purportedly show him making inflammatory remarks about Muslims and government critics. In others, he boasts about his political connections and claims he does not fear arrest.His online presence suggests that the persona seen in the viral clip was not an isolated episode, but part of a broader public image he had cultivated over time.On Thursday, a day before his detention, Bhardwaj shared a screenshot showing his name among the trends on X, captioning it, "Love you all Virodhi".He also posted a photograph on Instagram showing a 'kada' on his wrist with the caption "Feel the power!". The post appeared to reference a Delhi Police statement that Kumar had been injured by a 'kada' and "not by any weapon".His social media accounts also featured photographs with political leaders, including Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra and Union minister Chirag Paswan.Paswan said on Friday that Bhardwaj had misused his name and the names of other leaders.The Union minister for food processing industries said he had lodged a complaint against Bhardwaj and demanded action against him."No action despite the accused admitting to an attack that could have been fatal sets a bad example; I take responsibility for ensuring justice for the family," Paswan said.Bhardwaj's accounts also included what appeared to be AI-generated images of him with women wearing burqas or hijabs.One particularly violent image, posted on 22 May, showed Bhardwaj holding the bloodied chin of a man. The accompanying text referred to "Mughal" and included the words "aa gaya swad".His Instagram account, which had around 184,000 followers, was deactivated on Friday. He also has a verified account on X with more than 6,400 followers.The viral video intensified demands for action against Bhardwaj, with protesters raising the issue during the CJP demonstration in Delhi on Friday.Police subsequently deployed several teams to trace him.According to police officials, Bhardwaj had travelled to Bulandshahr and was staying in Naithla village. He allegedly fled the village on a motorcycle towards Khurja before a police team could apprehend him.He was wearing a helmet, apparently in an attempt to conceal his identity, police said.Local residents told TOI that Bhardwaj had arrived in Bulandshahr early on Friday, allegedly to evade arrest, and had taken shelter at the home of a local family.While there, he interacted with some journalists and reportedly repeated his claims about the alleged assault during the CJP protest.Bhardwaj was staying at the house of Harishankar Sharma, a Naithla resident who works as a cab driver in the Delhi-NCR region.Sharma said he had met Bhardwaj during an earlier journey.“Bhardwaj called me and said he wanted to come to my house to meet me. He arrived early in the morning along with another man. Initially, I did not suspect anything. But when media persons started arriving at my village, I sensed something was wrong,” Sharma said.Sharma said Bhardwaj later asked to borrow his motorcycle, saying he would return “within five minutes”.“Then I came to know that Delhi Police had detained him. It was only after that I learnt that he was wanted in a criminal case in the national capital. I still do not know much about the case,” Sharma said.The detention came after CJP representatives said Delhi Police had assured them that Bhardwaj “will be arrested within 72 hours”.The case has since drawn attention not only to the alleged assault but also to the online persona Bhardwaj had built through provocative posts, political associations and claims of influence.
Article Summary: Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday. He is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20. His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which he claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the father.

Article Title: Amazon techie leaves Rs 46 lakh package to join Indian Army, set to be commissioned at OTA Gaya
Article Text:
Shardendu Tiwari





LUCKNOW: Lucknow’s 27-year-old Shardendu Tiwari, who worked as a cloud engineer at Amazon with an annual package of around Rs 46 lakh, is set to be commissioned into the Army at the Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, on Saturday.A second-generation soldier, Shardendu chose military service after leaving behind a corporate career and an opportunity with global aerospace company Airbus. His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces.Shardendu resides in Neelmatha, Lucknow, and his family traces its roots to Pipergaon in Sultanpur district. His father, Honorary Captain Raj Kumar Tiwari, served in the Army Service Corps for 36 years before retiring. Inspired by his father, Shardendu developed an inclination towards joining the armed forces during his childhood.He completed his schooling at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Chandimandir, Haryana. He pursued a Bachelor of Engineering degree in Information Technology and later completed an MTech in Computer Science and Information Security from Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh.Shardendu appeared for Army selection eight times before succeeding.He joined through the technical entry route, which enabled him to serve in the Army while remaining connected with technology.“I was also drawn to the armed forces because of the opportunities they offer for adventure and field service,” he said.During training at OTA Gaya, his leadership qualities earned him the appointment of Senior Under Officer (SUO), one of the highest cadet appointments at the academy. He enjoys playing basketball and table tennis.

His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces. Article Title: Hours after AAIB report, AI sacks Phuket flight pilot
Article Text:
Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi

Software malfunction or manual intervention? Final report may reveal

NEW DELHI: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight hours after Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test". Terming this confirmation a "serious concern", AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance" on "priority" in its interim safety recommendations and conclusion. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had soon after this accident asked DGCA chief Vir Vikram Yadav to make dope rules more stringent.AI was considering action, including termination, against the PIC for some weeks now but was awaiting AAIB's prelim report into what has now been categorised as an "accident" due to its severity and impact. An AI spokesperson said: "Safety remains AI's highest priority. In line with AI's zero-tolerance approach to violation of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements, the pilot's employment has been terminated with immediate effect. "When the badly rattled Airbus A320 had landed in Delhi with 24 injured people and a damaged aircraft cabin, both the pilots were subjected to post-flight breath-analyser examination as per standard protocol.They cleared that test.But for some reason which may be disclosed in the final report, the unusual step of conducting dope tests was taken in this case. “The sample of PIC was found non-negative. Blood samples of both the flight crew were sent to path lab for confirmatory (dope) test. The confirmatory test report of PIC was found non-negative whereas the sample of co-pilot was found negative in both the tests,” stated the interim report.An AAIB probe is on to find what caused the Airbus A320 to suffer an extremely rare failure of all three hydraulic systems within seconds. The final report is expected to reveal whether it happened due to something going wrong with the aircraft’s hardware or software or whether due to some manual intervention with the PIC having some role in that, if any. Hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels.Such was the impact of this “event” which happened that 24 people got injured and the aircraft cabin saw significant damage, including a lavatory commode getting uprooted from its location. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken and sealing panel found dislocated near the tenth row. The forward right side emergency exit handle was found broken.The cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and crew. The crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision of continuing the flight to its destination Delhi and not diverting to the nearest en route airport.Following the report, AI said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India’s highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements. Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.” “The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements,” Air India’s statement added.
Article Summary: Air India Friday sacked the pilot-in-command of its badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket- Delhi flight. Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau's preliminary report concluded the "PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory (dope) test" AAIB has asked Directorate General of Civil Aviation to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit"

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi vs C Joseph Vijay: Can TVK chief do what Arvind Kejriwal could not?
Article Text:
Vijay's national ambitions: Can the TVK chief succeed where Kejriwal failed?

Vijay's extraordinary first step

Vijay emerged as the disrupter-in-chief in Tamil Nadu elections.

Congress leader on TVK's 'Vijay-for-PM' pitch.

The 'agnipath' of Vijay's path

Rahul Gandhi's political journey.

Can Tamil Nadu be Vijay’s launchpad?

BJP has used the opportunity to question TVK-Congress alliance.

Why Congress cannot simply step aside

The Kejriwal test

Vijay's one-point lead on Kejriwal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The honeymoon period between Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and its coalition partner, the Congress, appears to be over. Barely months after the two parties came together to form the government, they are already sparring over a question that is ostensibly about the 2029 Lok Sabha election: Who should be the opposition's prime ministerial face - Rahul Gandhi or Vijay?What began as statements and counter-statements between the two party leaders has quickly acquired a sharper political edge.TVK PWD minister Aadhav Arjuna pitched Vijay as a potential national leader, arguing that the country's highest political office should go to a leader from Tamil Nadu. On the other hand, state minister S Rajesh Kumar said Congress ministers in the Tamil Nadu cabinet would resign if TVK did not support Rahul Gandhi as the PM candidate in 2029.The confrontation spilled into the assembly as well. Congress Legislature Party leader and MLA Tharahai Cuthbert was shifted on August 31 from the section allotted to TVK legislators to the front row of the opposition benches.But beneath the immediate fight over Rahul versus Vijay lies a much bigger question: Does Vijay intend to remain a powerful Tamil Nadu leader, or does he see the state's 2026 mandate as the launchpad for a national political project?And if the latter is the plan, can he succeed where Arvind Kejriwal could not?The scale of Vijay's rise explains why the 2029 debate has surfaced so early.The April 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly election ended nearly six decades of dominance by the DMK and AIADMK.TVK, only two years old, emerged as the largest party with 108 seats in the 234-member assembly. The DMK won 59 and AIADMK 47, while Congress secured five seats, with the remaining seats going to smaller allies.TVK was therefore not merely a new party that performed better than expected. It emerged as the central political force in an election that disrupted the state's traditional two-party equilibrium.There was, however, one problem: 108 seats were still short of the 118 required for a simple majority.That made Congress indispensable.Vijay eventually formed the government with the support of MLAs from Congress [5], VCK [2] and IUML [2], along with outside support from the Left parties [4]. The MDMK, which has two MLAs, later extended its support.Congress moved away from its long-standing association with the DMK and backed a TVK-led government along with smaller allies, taking the coalition's strength to 121. Vijay was sworn in as CM on May 10.Congress had submitted its letter of support after the election, making it clear that its support would be conditional on TVK keeping "communal forces" out of the alliance.The 234-member assembly currently has seven vacancies following the resignation of six AIADMK MLAs and Vijay vacating his second seat, Trichy East. The effective strength of the House is therefore 227, bringing the majority mark down to 114.The political equation is unusual. Congress is the junior partner, with only five seats, but its support helped Vijay cross the majority mark. At the same time, TVK's 108 seats give Vijay overwhelming dominance within the coalition.That inversion may be at the heart of the present tension.Congress had been with the DMK in the pre-poll alliance and had never secured a place in MK Stalin's cabinet. After the results, however, it quickly moved to TVK's side and helped Vijay form the government.The alliance therefore contains a built-in contradiction: the party that needs Vijay's government to survive does not want Vijay to emerge as the leader of the national opposition.Vijay's route to Delhi runs into a problem that no amount of success in Tamil Nadu can entirely solve: numbers.Tamil Nadu sends 39 MPs to the Lok Sabha. Even a TVK sweep in 2029 would leave Vijay nowhere close to the 272 seats needed for a majority in the 543-member House.History, however, offers a little hope.In the past, India has had PMs whose parties did not come close to a Lok Sabha majority. HD Deve Gowda became PM in 1996 after the Janata Dal won just 46 seats, emerging as the consensus choice of the United Front with Congress support. IK Gujral followed a year later under much the same arrangement, with the Janata Dal holding only around 45 seats. Chandra Shekhar became prime minister in 1990 after breaking away from the Janata Dal with just 64 MPs, relying on outside support from Congress.This may give Vijay some hope.But it is also where the historical comparison begins to fray. The coalition politics that made these leaders PMs belonged to a different national landscape where coalition governments were a norm. The BJP, however, has changed that equation, building the NDA into a durable national coalition rather than the loose, post-election arrangements that defined much of the 1990s.The opposition, meanwhile, has come together in the form of the INDIA bloc which Vijay's TVK is not part of yet.And yet, paradoxically, being outside the INDIA bloc may give Vijay an advantage over Rahul Gandhi.Rahul comes with the weight of the Congress's history: its national footprint, its alliances and rivalries, the Nehru-Gandhi legacy and the political resistance that the party can provoke among regional leaders. Vijay comes with much less baggage. He would enter a coalition conversation not as the leader of a decades-old national party, but as a new political force with a mass following built before he entered politics.That distinction could matter if the next Lok Sabha produces another fractured mandate. But that is a big if, and one that looks unlikely in the present circumstances.Congress MP Karti Chidambaram has already put the arithmetic bluntly: "Every party has dreams, ambitions, and desires ... but we know what the political reality is. There are 543 constituencies."Thus, for Vijay, even if his party manages to sweep all 39 Tamil Nadu seats, the real test would be in finding enough allies to make Delhi possible.There is, however, one route Vijay could attempt that would give his national project a distinct political identity.He could build around Tamil Nadu's distinctive relationship with the Centre and a broader southern assertion in national politics — the argument that Delhi needs a stronger voice from a region that has historically resisted political and cultural centralisation.That could give TVK's national project a political argument beyond Vijay's celebrity and the anti-incumbency against established parties.But it comes with its own problem.A political identity rooted in Tamil pride and southern assertion may work strongly in Tamil Nadu, but it does not automatically translate into votes in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal or other states.Vijay would therefore have to balance two identities: the Tamil leader whose legitimacy comes from Tamil Nadu and the national leader who must persuade voters elsewhere that his politics is not confined to the state.For Congress, the dispute is not simply about Rahul Gandhi's personal ambitions or the future of the Gandhi family. It is about whether the party can retain its position as the principal national pole of the opposition after years of organisational and electoral decline.Rahul has spent years positioning himself as the principal challenger to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP. Congress's improved performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha election and Rahul's emergence as leader of opposition strengthened that claim.The subsequent assembly elections, however, have weakened the party's position against the BJP.A recent survey placing Rahul as the second-most preferred PM choice and Vijay next is nevertheless significant. Vijay's position is remarkable for a leader whose party has contested only one assembly election, even though such surveys are hardly a substitute for actual elections.For Congress, conceding the national leadership question to Vijay now would risk allowing another regional leader to occupy the political space the party is trying to reclaim, especially after the weakened positioning of Mamata Banerjee, MK Stalin and Kejriwal.Kejriwal also began with an extraordinary political breakthrough in a single territory before attempting to turn his party into a national alternative.When he launched the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in November 2012, his political project was built around challenging established parties, particularly Congress, which had governed Delhi for 15 years under Sheila Dikshit.AAP's breakthrough came almost immediately. Kejriwal became CM in December 2013, resigned after 49 days and returned in February 2015 with one of the most emphatic mandates in Indian electoral politics: AAP won 67 of Delhi's 70 assembly seats, reducing Congress to zero.But Kejriwal did not intend to stop at Delhi.The 2014 Lok Sabha election was his first major attempt to build a national footprint. AAP contested 432 seats and won four, all in Punjab. Kejriwal himself challenged Narendra Modi in Varanasi, while Kumar Vishwas contested Amethi against Rahul Gandhi. Neither challenge produced the national breakthrough AAP was seeking.The party then entered the Punjab and Goa assembly elections in 2017. Punjab became a second political laboratory, with AAP winning 20 of 117 seats and emerging as the principal opposition force behind Congress. Goa, however, exposed the limits of the expansion strategy, with AAP failing to win a single assembly seat.Punjab eventually provided the big breakthrough. In the 2022 election, AAP won 92 of 117 seats and formed a government under Bhagwant Mann.Kejriwal had therefore achieved something genuinely difficult: he had built governments in two states and turned AAP into a recognisable political force beyond Delhi.Yet the national leap remained elusive.AAP's electoral strength outside its core states never matched the scale of its Delhi and Punjab victories. In Gujarat, where it tried to establish itself as a third force, the party won five assembly seats in 2022, while Goa remained marginal. Its Lok Sabha presence also remained modest.The Tamil Nadu CM has one advantage over Kejriwal though that their starting points are different.Kejriwal had to build a mass political identity almost from scratch. Vijay, however, spent decades building one through cinema before entering politics. He then converted that popularity into 108 assembly seats in his very first election, which was dubbed as an extraordinary political conversion.But it can also become a weakness.The question is no longer whether millions of people know Vijay. They do.The question is whether voters who know him as an actor and Tamil Nadu CM will vote for TVK in states where the party has no political history, local leadership or cadre network.To go national, Vijay would need candidates, local leaders, a cadre network and alliances. Most importantly, he would need a political proposition that resonates with voters who do not know him primarily as a Tamil film star.This is where Kejriwal's experience matters most.AAP's success in Delhi could not simply be reproduced across the country. Punjab offered a favourable political opening, but Goa and Gujarat demonstrated that national visibility and electoral organisation are very different things.Vijay's task could be even harder because many of the states he would need to enter already have powerful regional leaders with their own political ambitions.For now, the 2029 PM debate may therefore be premature, but the political conflict it has exposed is not. Vijay may need Congress to consolidate the power he has won in Tamil Nadu even as he seeks to challenge Congress's claim to national opposition leadership.That is the paradox at the heart of his political project.If Vijay can use the Congress alliance to build a durable organisation without becoming politically dependent on it, he may have found a route Kejriwal could not. But if TVK's national ambitions remain ahead of its organisational reach, the 2029 debate could end up looking less like the beginning of a national challenge and more like the first sign of a regional party reaching beyond its electoral weight.
Article Summary: Vijay emerged as the disrupter-in-chief in Tamil Nadu elections. Congress is the junior partner, with only five seats, but its support helped Vijay cross the majority mark. At the same time, TVK seats give Vijay overwhelming dominance within the coalition.

Article Title: Air India Phuket-Delhi incident: All 3 hydraulic systems failed; pilot tested positive for psychoactive substance
Article Text:
The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window. VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: The preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet, triggering an autopilot disengagement, stall warning and an altitude upset. Alongside the technical findings, the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has recommended that the DGCA take action against the Pilot-in-Command, who tested non-negative for psychoactive substance use following the flight."The confirmation of use of psycho-active substance is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority," the report said. The interim safety recommendation asked the regulator to "take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psycho-active substance." Post-flight, both pilots underwent a breath analyser test, which came back satisfactory. But the subsequent psychoactive substance detection test returned a non-negative result for the PIC, a finding confirmed by a follow-up laboratory blood test. The co-pilot tested negative on both counts.The hydraulic failure itself, the more immediate cause of the injuries onboard, unfolded within a five-second window.VT-EXO, an eight-year-old A320neo carrying 145 people, had just been cleared to climb from FL340 to FL360 after entering Kolkata Flight Information Region. At 04:02:43 UTC, the flight control system "detected loss of green hydraulic system." Four seconds later, the flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of Blue and Yellow hydraulic systems. With all three systems compromised simultaneously, the autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet from its assigned level, the report said.The co-pilot, who was Pilot Flying, responded first to the upset before the captain took over the controls. Recovery was swift. "At around 04:02:52 UTC, the Blue hydraulic system was recovered, and a few seconds later, the Yellow hydraulic and the Green hydraulic systems were also recovered," the report said. It restored normal flight control surfaces within seconds of the failure.But with seatbelt signs off during cruise, the sudden upset threw passengers and crew around the cabin. Twenty-four people, including four cabin crew, needed medical attention on landing; four were hospitalised with serious injuries. The cabin damage was extensive: cracked ceiling panels across multiple rows, dislodged overhead bins, a broken emergency exit handle, a lavatory commode "uprooted from its original location," and a bent crew seat. Despite the injuries, the flight crew chose not to divert, opting instead to continue to Delhi while requesting medical priority from ATC. The aircraft landed safely on runway 11L at 05:30 UTC, around ninety minutes after the failure.Investigators have already flagged one detail for closer scrutiny: the aircraft was dispatched from Phuket under an active Minimum Equipment List item for the Power Transfer Unit, invoked a week earlier on July 28. The PTU serves as an auxiliary hydraulic source shared between the green and yellow systems, and its status at the time of the failure is expected to be a focus of the ongoing probe. Flight recorder data has been downloaded and is under analysis, and a technical team from Airbus and France's BEA inspected the aircraft in Delhi in mid-August, after which hydraulic components and fluid samples were removed for further testing.“The Airbus A320 aircraft has three hydraulic systems. They are identified as the green, blue and yellow systems. Together they supply hydraulic power at 3000 psi (206 bar) to the main power users. Services which are not used during flight are isolated from the main supply. Hydraulic fluid cannot be transferred from one system to another. Each system has its own hydraulic reservoir,” the report said, explaining the hydraulics on the aircraft.On the green system, the normal source of pressure is the Engine Driven Pump (EDP) located on the left engine and, as an auxiliary source, the Power Transfer Unit (PTU). On the blue system, the normal source of pressure is the electrical pump (E-Pump) and, as an auxiliary source, the Ram Air Turbine (RAT). On the yellow system, the normal source of pressure is the EDP located on the right engine and as auxiliary sources the PTU and the electric pump (E-Pump). “Each hydraulic system pressurisation information is available for the aircraft systems through one pressure transmitter (numerical value of the pressure), two pressure switches (discrete value indicating if there is a loss of pressure). Relevant Hydraulic components were removed from the aircraft for further analysis,” the report said. The PTU is an auxiliary pressure supply for either the green or yellow systems without transfer of fluid between the two systems. It operates automatically if there is a delta pressure of 500 psi between the green/yellow or yellow/green hydraulic systems, it addedThe said report is preliminary, and a detailed technical investigation is still underway.
Article Summary: Preliminary investigation into the August 4 Air India Phuket-Delhi accident has found that the aircraft's three hydraulic systems, green, blue and yellow, lost pressure within seconds while the A320 was cruising at 36,000 feet. Autopilot disengaged, a continuous repetitive chime sounded, and the stall warning triggered for two seconds. The aircraft "encountered altitude upset," gaining 372 feet before falling 292 feet.

Article Title: RSS says of critics of Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip: ‘Let them speak, we’re open to dialogue’
Article Text:
RSS spokesman Sunil Ambekar in London for Mohan Bhagwat visit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

LONDON: The RSS shrugged off criticism by civil groups of its chief Dr Mohan Bhagwat’s UK trip, saying in a democracy differences of opinions are expected and “should not be taken as a shock”.The RSS head arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour, having just visited New York and Toronto on a “dialogue mission.”Hindus for Human Rights UK and several other campaign groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit, pointing out New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani had done that.Labour PIO MP Nadia Whittome tabled a written parliamentary question asking the home office whether “the visit engages the commitment to block hate preachers and extremists from entering the UK”.“We are here for peace, integration and oneness and we are open for dialogue with everyone. In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices. We are engaging with those who wish to dialogue with us,” RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.“We are here to communicate what we are and how we think. We are very much open. We have nothing to hide. We expect a debate and exchange of thoughts. Let them speak.”On allegations the RSS was behind the 2022 Leicester riots, Ambekar said this was a “UK domestic issue”. “There is no question… RSS was not involved. Already people are finding out their legal options. Hindus are a peace-loving community.”He said there are a lot of “misconceptions” in the West. “Bharat is not a nation state political concept — it is a cultural concept. Hindutva is not like any religion — it’s a concept where there will be respect for all religious practices. That is Hindutva, and that is Bharat, so I think the trip will help to clear the ideas,” he said.A spokesperson for the London mayor said the mayor “does not have the power” to ban people from speaking. “London is proud to celebrate our diversity and intolerance has no place in our great city,” the spokesperson said.
Article Summary: Mohan Bhagwat arrived in London on Sept 2 on the final leg of his three-city outreach RSS centenary tour. Civil groups wrote an open letter to London mayor Sadiq Khan asking him to condemn the visit. “In a democracy, it is very normal to raise different voices,” RSS head of media Sunil Ambekar said at a press briefing on Friday.

Article Title: Ladakh residents to get ownership rights over 60,000 acres of barren land
Article Text:
Ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: Ladakh residents will now have rights over barren lands or wastelands owned by govt, with the administration Friday approving Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Nautor Regularisation) Rules, 2026.The Rules provide a comprehensive framework for granting proprietary rights on up to 10 acres of eligible Nautor land holdings to the occupants across all seven districts of the Union Territory. For Nautor land beyond the 10-acre limit, the proprietary rights may be allotted on a leasehold basis, in accordance with the rules.Nautor land refers to barren or wasteland, owned by govt, which was earlier allotted to individuals for cultivation or other productive use. More than 60,000 acres of land in Ladakh is presently recorded in revenue records as Nautor holdings.The Rules offer a one-time regularisation mechanism for Nautor land, occupied before the repeal of J&K Tenancy Act-980, on Oct 27, 2020. Any possession of Nautor land after this cut-off date will be ineligible for regularisation.“The Nautor issue has a deep historical connection with the lives and livelihoods of the people of Ladakh.For generations, our people have worked hard to bring barren and waste land under cultivation in one of the most challenging agricultural environments in the country. These Rules provide a transparent and uniform mechanism to address this long-pending issue and give legal certainty to genuine holders. It will also enable such land to be utilised as a financial asset, including for availing bank loans,” Ladakh LG Vinai Kumar Saxena said.According to the Rules, the authority of allotting Nautor land will be vested in Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils in all seven districts.A govt spokesperson said the absence of a clear and uniform legal framework until now restricted the effective utilisation of Nautor land. “In particular, landholders with limited or non-proprietary rights, were unable to use the land as a financial asset, including for purposes such as obtaining loans against it. At the same time, the absence of uniform rules also posed a threat of claims and disputes over govt, council land,” the spokesperson said.

Article Title: Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis
Article Text:
File photo of Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal.

BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reiterated that the party is preparing to contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats.

BJP's message: We can do it alone

But the doors don't seem completely shut

Akalis have not been subtle about wanting alliance with BJP

Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal's remarks added to speculation over a possible revival of ties.

Akalis need BJP more than before

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann accused the Akali Dal of seeking a reunion with the BJP for political power.

Why BJP may have kept the door open

But does BJP actually need the Akalis?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Is the BJP playing hardball with the Akalis in Punjab ? Yet another senior BJP leader has announced that the party will contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab on its own strength.BJP national general secretary Satish Poonia, in his first media interaction after being appointed the party's organisational in-charge for Punjab, made it clear that the message from the central leadership was to prepare for all 117 constituencies in the state. He also sought to play down Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month, saying meetings between political leaders should not automatically be read as signs of an alliance.Poonia is not the first senior BJP leader to reiterate the 'solo contest' point.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh had earlier told party functionaries in Punjab that the BJP would contest all 117 assembly seats independently.And yet, the speculation of an alliance between the two parties refuses to go away.The question then is whether the BJP is really shutting the door on its old ally or raising the bar before any possible deal.The BJP today has reasons to sound more confident than it did when both parties went their separate ways.The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies while the SAD remained the dominant force in the alliance.In the 2017 assembly election, the last Punjab polls the two parties contested together, the SAD fought 94 seats and the BJP just 23. The BJP won three and the Akalis 15.This arrangement will clearly no longer work for the BJP.Since splitting with the Akalis, the BJP has been working towards a plan. The party has been trying to expand beyond its old pockets in Punjab, in line with its national growth, and build an independent base. The West Bengal victory has indeed strengthened the confidence within the party. Punjab BJP leaders have also publicly argued that the party's improved vote share and national presence have strengthened the case for fighting the elections independently.That makes the repeated declaration of contesting 117 seats more than just a message to the Akalis. It is also a message to BJP workers that the party intends to build its own organisation across Punjab.Interestingly, even in the middle of this high-pitched rhetoric, the Student Organisation of India (SOI), which is the students’ wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal, extended support to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidate in the Panjab University Campus Students’ Council elections and helped its candidate win the presidential post.The SOI offered this olive branch to BJP’s student wing a day before the voting and helped ABVP create a record of winning the top post in the students’ council election for the second time in a row.This campus politics bonhomie was significant messaging. The Akalis, who had walked away from the decades-old alliance with the BJP in 2020 over the now-repealed farm bills, have dropped very clear and open hints that they desperately want to revive the ties.There have been a series of overtures from their end to seek an alliance without expressing that in as many words.If the BJP is keeping its cards close to its chest, the Akalis have been far more open about it.The PM Modi-Sukhbir Badal meeting was perhaps the beginning of this outreach. It was their first one-on-one political meeting since the SAD walked out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020 over the three farm laws, ending an alliance that had lasted nearly two decades.Days after this meeting, the SAD reversed its stand on the Delimitation Bill and announced its support for the constitutional amendment bill which the BJP is trying to pass in Parliament. This was a huge U-turn that prompted digs from the ruling AAP and the Congress over the SAD’s desperation for an alliance with the BJP.The shift in stance drew attention because the party had earlier taken a much more critical position on delimitation. The SAD had in April stated in Lok Sabha that the BJP was repeatedly changing the goal post on women's reservation and decried that the delimitation exercise was being conducted in the garb of the Women's Reservation Bill.Then came more signals from within the Akali leadership.Senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia went public advocating an alliance, and said that people want SAD and the BJP to come together for peace, development and progress of Punjab.Majithia's statement came after his sister and former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal stoked fresh speculation about a re-alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP by expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that carried progress to Punjab from Delhi.None of these statements amounted to a formal alliance proposal. However, they made it clear that the Akali leadership was increasingly interested in reviving ties with the BJP.The reason is not difficult to see. The Akalis have been pushed to the fringes of Punjab politics.Its vote share and seat share have declined in the last few elections. In fact, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP managed a huge lead over SAD in terms of vote share.The BJP secured 18.56% of the votes but failed to win a parliamentary seat in Punjab. The Akali Dal, despite winning Bathinda, finished with 13.42% vote share.The BJP also finished ahead of SAD candidates across several constituencies and led in 24 assembly segments. In the 2022 assembly polls, by comparison, the BJP's vote share was only around 6.6%, while SAD was a little over 18%.That perhaps explains why the Akalis seem desperate for an alliance. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has claimed that the Shiromani Akali Dal leadership is "on its knees" to forge an alliance with the BJP and return to power in the state to "loot" it again.So, the big question is: why is the BJP acting tough? Is it against reviving the alliance with the Akalis? Or is the BJP just playing hardball to ensure that it is the “big brother” in any future alliance?For the Akalis, the decline has been much more painful.Akalis, who dominated Punjab politics for years, were reduced to three seats in the 2022 assembly election and one Lok Sabha seat in 2024. Now, the party has to compete not only with the Congress but also with AAP, which swept the last state election, and also a BJP trying to expand independently.That perhaps explains the urgency.When BJP and SAD were in alliance earlier, there was little ambiguity about who was the senior partner.The SAD had more seats and more say in deciding the assembly seats and the chief ministerial candidate. The BJP accepted most terms because the arrangement perhaps gave the BJP a space where its independent visibility was limited.But now, if there is an alliance between the two again, it surely will be on completely different terms.The BJP has spent the years since the split trying to build an identity of its own in Punjab. It has brought leaders from other parties into its fold, expanded its organisation and fielded candidates across the entire state in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.Even in recent weeks, it has continued inducting figures from outside the party as it prepares for the assembly contest.For the BJP, therefore, returning to an arrangement in which it simply receives around 20-odd seats would be difficult. This is perhaps where the bargaining may be happening. Therefore, the real question might just be if the Akalis are willing to accept the changed political reality.There is another reason why the BJP may be keeping the Akalis guessing.Declaring an alliance too early could derail BJP's bid to strengthen its organisation in the state build an independent identity. Keeping the 117-seat option alive allows the BJP to continue expanding and encouraging its cadres.The BJP knows the Akalis are willing to return. There is little reason for the BJP to make any commitment before discussing seats and leadership.The public posturing notwithstanding, the BJP also stands to gain from a possible alliance. The BJP's 18.56% vote share in the Lok Sabha election did not translate into a single seat. This shows that the party did expand its base, but that vote share by itself may not be enough.The Akalis, meanwhile, still have traditional pockets of support. That gives both sides something the other may want.Fighting independently gives it the freedom to contest every region, develop new leaders and try to move beyond its traditional urban base. Even an election in which it improves substantially without forming the government could further that objective. An alliance with SAD could interrupt that process.Also, the Sikh community's identity continues to play an important role in Punjab politics. For the BJP, a renewed alliance with the Akali Dal could help it reach sections of Sikh voters and rural Punjab where the party has traditionally struggled to build a strong independent base.For now, the two sides appear to be speaking in very different registers.The Akalis have repeatedly sent signals that they are willing to reopen the relationship. The BJP is listening but not reacting. For now, all BJP leaders are maintaining that the party is preparing for all 117 seats.Yet the Modi-Sukhbir meeting, the SOI-ABVP cooperation and reports of discussions behind the scenes mean the possibility of an alliance cannot be written off either.It is possible that the BJP means exactly what it says and will go into the election alone. But if the two former allies do eventually come together, it is unlikely to be a return to the partnership that existed before 2020.The fight, therefore, may not just be about whether BJP and SAD become allies again. It may be about who gets to be the 'big brother' this time.
Article Summary: BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh reiterated that the party is preparing to contest all 117 Punjab assembly seats. The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies.

Article Title: Work hard, own the world
Article Text:
may there always be enough for everyone.

Nediyon

Ulagalandhaan

“Madiyila Mannavan Eydhum Adialandhaan

Thaaya Dhellam Orungu.”

never underestimate the power of someone who appears unassuming. When the right moment comes, every Vamana may blossom into a Trivikrama.

Last week, I was in London and had a day to myself. I decided to visit the Sherlock Holmes Museum. Sherlock Holmes has always been a favourite character of mine. As is often the case in London, getting to the station, followed by two train rides. It was quite a journey, but entirely worth it.On my return, hunger took over. I was delighted when my host suggested a South Indian restaurant. I asked for a dosa .“Not available.” The only item on the menu was Onam sadhya.Of course, it was Onam.And suddenly, the absence of a dosa seemed like a blessing.A sadhya is not merely a meal. It is a celebration of abundance. Sitting in a corner of London, with thoran, erissery and jackfruit payasam before me, felt less like eating and more like being transported to heaven.Onam celebrates the annual return of King Mahabali to visit his people in Kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. The sadhya seems to embody the spirit of his kingdom:That thought took me to another story—that of Vamana , who became Trivikrama. The image at its core—the three cosmic strides of Vishnu—is much older. In the Rigveda, Vishnu is celebrated as the deity who takes three great steps across the universe. It is interesting that the names Rama and Krishna find little mention in the early scriptures, but Trivikrama is omnipresent; both in scriptures and literature, even in ancient Tamil literature. Sangam works such as Paripadal, Kalithogai and Perumpaanatrupadai evoke Vishnu asor—the One who measured the worlds.There is even an ancient tradition connecting the origin of the River Vaigai with this cosmic act. When Trivikrama raised his foot and pierced the upper worlds, Brahma is said to have washed that divine foot. The sacred water that flowed down towards Earth became associated with the Vaigai. Myth, landscape and poetry became woven together.Early Tamil poetry was deeply conscious of landscape, boundaries and celestial order. A God who could cross the limits of the universe with a single stride was a magnificent poetic image.And Thiruvalluvar, who rarely invokes deities directly, chose precisely this image in the Thirukkural .In the chapter on freedom from laziness, he says in Kural 610:“A king who is completely free from laziness will gain all that wasMeasured by the feet of Trivikrama.”The grandeur of the image is striking. Trivikrama measured the worlds with his feet; Valluvar transforms that into a metaphor for human effort. The energetic can reach whatever vastness the universe may contain. What seems beyond one’s grasp may become attainable when one refuses to be held back by indolence. And there is another thought in this transformation from Vamana to Trivikrama:And perhaps that was the unexpected journey I experienced at London: from Sherlock Holmes to an Onam sadhya, to Mahabali, and from Mahabali to Trivikrama; my friend and I travelled quite a lot for the dosa we didn’t get. My takeaway was; don’t be upset if you don’t get what you wanted: you may end up with much more!
Article Summary: Onam celebrates the annual return of King Mahabali to visit his people in Kerala. His reign is remembered as an age of prosperity, equality and generosity. The sadhya seems to embody the spirit of his kingdom. That thought took me to another story—that of Vamana, who became Trivikrama.

Article Title: Punjab government to hike DA of 85,000 employees from 42 to 60 pc: Minister Aman Arora
Article Text:
