Chandigarh, Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday.Speaking to mediapersons here, Arora said a recommendation in this regard was made by the Cabinet Sub-Committee formed to examine the issues of employees.The announcement is significant as employees recruited after July 17, 2020 were getting a pay equivalent to the Central pay scales, along with 42 per cent Dearness Allowance (DA). These were much lower than the pay scales of employees recruited before July 2020, who were paid as per the Punjab Pay Commission.Arora said there were two pay scales in Punjab, which was leading to conflicting interests and confusion: the Punjab basic pay scales and the one equivalent to the Central basic pay scales (as per the 7th Central Pay Commission)."Punjab basic pay scales, which traditionally are higher, range from 30 to 70 per cent more than the Central basic pay. And when DA is added to it, which is currently 42 per cent, the salary increases much above the Central pay scales," he said."When we calculate and compare, even with 60 per cent DA added to Central basic pay, the Punjab pay scales and take-home salaries are higher," he said.Arora said the previous Congress government had decided to hire employees on the Central pay scales after July 17, 2020.In the last six years, 85,000 employees have been recruited.The Mann government will give them a "Janmashtami gift" as the three-member Cabinet Sub-Committee has decided that the DA of these employees will be raised from 42 to 60 per cent. The committee's recommendation will be sent to the chief minister, Arora said.He, however, said that this hike will not benefit employees recruited before July 2020."From day one, the Bhagwant Mann government has been talking about the welfare of every section. We cannot imagine good governance without our employees," he said.The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including the release of their pending 18 per cent DA.They have also threatened to go on mass casual leave on September 8 if the state government does not withdraw a recent notice imposing disciplinary action against those who remained on "unauthorised absence" on August 27.The employees have given the state government time till September 7 to withdraw the notice issued to protesting employees.Punjab government on Thursday appealed to employee unions to engage with it through dialogue rather than confrontation, calling employees the backbone of good governance.
Article Summary: Punjab government will raise the Dearness Allowance of around 85,000 government employees recruited after July 17, 2020 by 18 per cent to 60 per cent, Cabinet Minister Aman Arora said on Friday. The development comes amid over 3 lakh government employees, who went on a statewide strike on August 27.

Article Title: SC overturns trial court, HC orders to acquit kidnap-murder accused
Article Text:
Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For the third time this week, Supreme Court freed a man sentenced by lower courts - in a kidnapping and murder case in the latest instance - questioning their analysis of evidence, and flagging loopholes in the prosecution theory tying the accused to the crime, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.A man was kidnapped in Telangana in 2012 and his father paid a ransom of Rs 1.5 lakh against a demand of Rs 23 lakh. His body was recovered from a fridge in a flat based on the disclosure of the accused, one of whom died during pendency of trial. A trial court convicted the five other accused. Telangana HC analysed evidence and acquitted four, but convicted one.The Supreme Court said barring the postmortem report indicating strangulation, and finding of the body, there was no substantive evidence to link the accused to the murder.Setting aside conviction and sentence, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said, “That victim died of ‘asphyxia due to smothering, associated with strangulation’, is established by the autopsy report and the dead body was detected, tucked away in a refrigerator inside an apartment. But for these, there is no scrap of evidence, worthy of reliance, to connect the six accused to the murder or even the flat.In another case, a man was accused of luring a boy with snacks to sodomise him. He was convicted by an Ambala court in April 2010 for the March 2007 “crime” of unnatural sex and murder, and given life term. Punjab and Haryana HC in Oct 2022 dismissed the appeal.A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva said police failed to conduct DNA test of the semen in the undergarment of the accused to match it with the rectal swab collected from victim’s undergarment. SC said the ‘last seen with’ theory is doubtful and that there were several missing links in the chain of the prosecution case. It acquitted the man, who had served 17 years in prison. The drawing of judicial curtains on the case had unpleasant outcomes: a man lost his young child to a crime which went unpunished, while a man unfairly convicted lost his prime years.In the third case, a murder in Bihar 25 years ago saw a trial court and Patna HC convict six persons. A bench of Justices Pardiwala and Chandran acquitted the convicts saying, “There is complete lack of evidence, and eyewitnesses testimonies do not inspire confidence… The case is not that of faulty investigation but of no probe having been carried out.

The Supreme Court said barring the postmortem report indicating strangulation, and finding of the body, there was no substantive evidence to link the accused to the murder.

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has directed National Testing Agency (NTA) to declare within 24 hours the NEET-UG re-examination results of two candidates, whose results were withheld over allegations linking them to the question paper leak. Justice Jasmeet Singh pointed out the candidates had not been named as accused by CBI in its chargesheet.While CBI told the court that it did not make them accused, though they had paid money to get question papers, the judge observed that at this stage, it was just an allegation and "therefore, the petitioners cannot be treated as persons against whom criminal culpability has been established or as having been found guilty of any illegality".The court was hearing the students' plea seeking release of their re-NEET results and permission to participate in the ongoing counselling. Article Title: Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics
Article Text:
Smoking raises mortality risk by 55% for diabetics

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups instead of being given a one-time "quit smoking" warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, represent the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type-2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses to people with diabetes.A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of their quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetics, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type-2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quitting strategies and relapse prevention.
Article Summary: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes. New international consensus calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type-2 diabetes care. Experts say patients should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-ups.

NEW DELHI: Broadening the definition of "property" under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, a special PMLA court in Mohali has ruled that seized bank cheques, even if not encashed, and narcotics both fall under the definition of "property" and constitute proceeds of crime under the money laundering Act.The judgement came Thursday, when ED launched a massive search operation at 30 premises across all zones of the southern region in different narcotics-related cases. The searches are being conducted under the mandate of Centre's 'Nasha Mukt Bharat' campaign with targets in the first phase spread across Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years, while rejecting the contention of the defence that their property and bank accounts were not attached and the seized contraband could not be considered proceeds of crime as no money trail had been brought on the record.Special judge Hardip Singh also rejected the defence's argument that the cheques recovered from the accused were not encashed and thus could not constitute proceeds of crime. The judge noted that the cheques were exchanged for the purpose of purchasing the contraband and the accused could not provide any explanation to the contrary.Starting with the four southern states, ED Thursday began a crackdown on major drug syndicates operating across the country.The drive has been launched as part of Centre's "drug-free India" campaign to attach properties of all those engaged in drug dealing and generation of "proceeds of crime". The ED's search covered targets involved in trafficking of illicit drugs like methamphetamine, marijuana, and MDMA. Over 20 foreign nationals are under scanner, an official said.Searches were conducted at premises in Chennai, Tirunelveli, Nagapattinam, Velankanni and Ramanathapuram in Tamil Nadu; Kolar, Malur (Kolar district) and Hoskote (Bengaluru North district); Serilingampally and Nanakramguda (Hyderabad) and Ranga Reddy district in Telangana; Kozhikode, Kannur, Malappuram and Thrissur in Kerala.ED is coordinating with other central agencies and state police forces that have registered cases of drug trafficking in the past few years to further investigate the money trail and track the proceeds of crime."The investigation prima facie discloses not merely trafficking of methamphetamine, but also the generation, receipt and movement of money arising out of this," a senior official said, adding that syndicates were using hawala and crypto currency dealers to further transfer the proceeds of crime outside the country to tax havens.The money trail to uncover cash-based hawala settlements revealed "account details, transaction records, diaries, slips or tokens, mobile phones, electronic communications and digital devices, property documents and other financial records". Based on these findings, the agency ascertained the complete quantum and trail of the proceeds of crime, and the persons who received, possessed, transferred, concealed, utilised or invested such proceeds.Further these details help in identifying movable and immovable properties acquired and that leads to their attachments.
Article Summary: A special PMLA court in Mohali has ruled that seized bank cheques, even if not encashed, and narcotics both fall under the definition of "property" The judgement came Thursday, when ED launched a massive search operation at 30 premises across all zones of the southern region in different narcotics-related cases. The judge convicted two accused and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for three years.

SRINAGAR: Mere possession of books with “dispiriting titles” does not make a person a criminal, the Jammu & Kashmir high court said, quashing an order for preventive detention of a man under the Public Safety Act (PSA) on charges of keeping and authoring books promoting separatist ideology.A single bench of Justice Moksha Khajuria Kazmi Thursday also observed that the PSA detention order passed by Kupwara district magistrate against the petitioner, Shafat Maqbool Wani, wrongly attributed to him the authorship of alleged anti-national literature seized from his house.Being a scholar, the petitioner could be expected to possess a variety of literary material, the court said, directing police to release Wani forthwith.Police claimed to have seized books with what they alleged were incriminating titles — ‘Construction of an Islamic Order in Hindutva Reimagination’ and ‘The Saffronization of occupied Kashmir, Demystifing Hindutva Settlers, Colonial Designers’ —from Wani’s house. They also attributed the authorship of the books to Wani.The court said the assertion that the detainee had inculcated a separatist ideology since his childhood as his father has been an ex-militant was “delusory”.“...The preventive detention, ordered so conveniently on such imaginary belief, is nothing but an unmindful exercise of power,” it observed.Justice Kazmi noted that the respondents had not shown any subversive activity against the petitioner that compelled them to take recourse to preventive detention.The HC ruling assumes significance as the home department banned the publication and circulation of 25 books on Kashmir, saying they promoted a “false narrative” and “secessionism”, on Aug 5, 2025, the sixth anniversary of abrogation of Article 370.The books include ‘Azadi’ by Arundhati Roy, ‘Kashmir: The Case for Freedom’, a collection of essays by Tariq Ali, Pankaj Mishra and others; ‘Confronting Terrorism’, also a collection of essays, edited by Maroof Raza; and ‘In Search of a Future’ by journalist and author David Devadas.The Kupwara DM ordered Wani’s detention under PSA on Sept 13, 2025, to prevent him from indulging in activities “detrimental to the security of the State”. The grounds cited included invitations he had received to attend some international conferences. The detention order came the same day he was granted bail by a Jammu NIA court in a UAPA case registered at Handwara police station.
Article Summary: Jammu & Kashmir high court quashes order for preventive detention of a man under the Public Safety Act (PSA) Shafat Maqbool Wani was accused of keeping and authoring books promoting separatist ideology. Police claimed to have seized books with what they alleged were incriminating titles.

Article Title: Jaishankar says India in touch with Russia, Ukraine to help end war

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Friday said India has been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia and is exploring whether ideas and suggestions can be developed to contribute to the mitigation and, ideally, the cessation of the conflict.Jaishankar made the remarks in Warsaw after holding talks with Poland's deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, a day after he met the top Ukrainian leadership in Kyiv.Addressing a joint press meet with Sikorski, Jaishankar said the two leaders discussed major global and regional issues, including the war in Ukraine, which is now in its fifth year.“The deputy Prime Minister and I also understandably discussed some major global and regional issues, notable among them is the war in Ukraine, now in its fifth year... I myself have just come here from Kyiv,” he said.Replying to a question, Jaishankar said India remained in touch with both sides.“What we are trying to do is to see if there are ideas and suggestions which can be developed in some way in which they will contribute to the mitigation, ideally, the cessation of the conflict,” he added.Jaishankar reiterated India's position that the conflict must end through dialogue and diplomacy.“India believes that endless war must give way to an end to war. These are wars without winners. Every additional day means more death, more destruction, more loss to the parties themselves, and more cost to the rest of the world,” he said.“Our efforts must therefore focus on promoting dialogue and diplomacy. We must each do what we can in whichever way we believe could be most effective and support the efforts of others to bring this conflict to an end. This is India's strong conviction, and we are acting on it,” he added.Responding to a question on India's purchases of Russian oil, Jaishankar said the solution to the conflict lay in negotiations rather than trade.“This war is not going to end... not because somebody chose to buy or not buy oil or alumina or fertilisers or metals and minerals. It will end when there is diplomacy, when there is dialogue and when there is negotiation. So, I think let's diagnose the problem right,” he said.A day earlier in Kyiv, Jaishankar had met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and foreign minister Andrii Sybiha and said India was ready to extend “any help in any manner” to help end the war.Following the meeting, Zelenskyy said he was “grateful to India for its commitment to ending this unjust war”.Jaishankar and Sikorski also discussed complex global challenges, including supply chain resilience and food, fuel and fertiliser security.The two ministers reviewed the progress of the India-Poland Joint Action Plan 2024-28, covering areas including trade and investment, space, digital technology, artificial intelligence, semiconductors, defence, education, shipping, mining and energy.Jaishankar also called on Polish President Karol Nawrocki and discussed the trajectory of the India-Poland Strategic Partnership, as well as the Ukraine conflict and developments in West Asia.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar said India has been in continuous touch with both Ukraine and Russia. He made the remarks in Warsaw after holding talks with Poland's deputy Prime Minister and foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. A day earlier he met the top Ukrainian leadership in Kyiv.

MATHURA: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath offered prayers at the historic Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple on Friday, participating in the Janmashtami celebrations and greeting devotees by showering flower petals.Addressing the occasion in Mathura, Adityanath underscored the timeless significance of Lord Krishna's teachings, asserting that teachings from millennia ago continue to guide society. The Uttar Pradesh CM noted that forces seeking to disrupt national unity, integrity, or faith will inevitably face the consequences outlined in sacred texts.He said, "The proclamations made by Lord Krishna over 5000 years ago remain just as relevant today. Its relevance is upheld by the principle of 'Paritranaya Sadhunam Vinashaya cha Dushkritam'; wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. However, regarding anti-national and anti-social forces that raise their heads to sow discord in society and attempt to harm India's unity, integrity, or faith, Lord Krishna had declared 5,000 years ago what their fate would be. "Highlighting the resilience of India's cultural heritage, the Chief Minister remarked that despite numerous historical invasions and attempts to suppress indigenous faiths, Sanatan Dharma has remained enduringly vibrant.He stated that those who dared to challenge or attempt to erase the tradition have vanished into oblivion."There were numerous invasions, and many attempted to impose their own faiths upon India, yet no one could erase the Sanatan Dharma. Those who had the audacity to try and obliterate the Sanatan Dharma were themselves reduced to dust and faded into oblivion. However, not only in Braj-bhoomi but across all of India, the memory of Shri Krishna and Radha Rserves as an inspiration for us today and fosters an atmosphere of enthusiasm and progress for future generations," Yogi Adityanath said.Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, lit up in colourful illuminations as the city celebrates Janmashtami, with temples and religious sites decorated.Meanwhile, on Friday, Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended greetings to the people on the occasion of Janmashtami, invoking Lord Krishna's teachings on selfless action and their enduring relevance.In a post on X, PM Modi wrote, "Heartfelt Janmashtami greetings to all of you. In the divine messages of Lord Shri Krishna lies the profound inspiration for selfless action, which has continuously guided humanity. May this sacred occasion, dedicated to his devotion and worship, infuse positive energy and strength into everyone's life-that is my heartfelt wish. Jai Shri Krishna!"Krishna Janmashtami, also known simply as Janmashtami or Gokulashtami, is an annual Hindu festival that celebrates the birth of Krishna, the eighth avatar of Vishnu. It is observed according to the Hindu luni-solar calendar, on the eighth day (Ashtami) of the Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) in the month of Bhadrapada, which overlaps with August and September of the Gregorian calendar.Meanwhile, devotees across the country are celebrating Janmashtami with religious fervour, gathering at temples for Mangla Aarti and special prayers to mark the birth of Lord Krishna.In Delhi, devotees gathered in large numbers at ISKCON temples in East of Kailash and Dwarka Sector 13 to participate in the Mangla Aarti held on the occasion of Janmashtami. Devotees joined the prayers and celebrated the festival at the temples.At the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Temple in Mathura, devotees took part in Mangala Aarti and special prayers as celebrations continued at the birthplace of Lord Krishna. People also danced and expressed their devotion to Lord Krishna.Mathura witnessed a particularly devotional atmosphere as devotees gathered at the temples across the city to participate in the religious ceremonies marking Janmashtami. The celebrations included prayers and rituals conducted at the temple, with devotees joining in the festivities.Religious celebrations and large gatherings have brought a festive atmosphere across the country as devotees come together to celebrate Janmashtami.

He directed officials to address practical difficulties arising in the implementation of pension schemes with sensitivity.The Chief Minister said the state government is regularly disbursing pensions to eligible beneficiaries through various social security pension schemes. He stressed the need to continuously work towards making the pension system simpler, transparent and beneficiary-centric, while ensuring that every eligible person is covered under the schemes.He further directed officials to identify eligible beneficiaries who are unable to obtain Aadhaar for any reason and make arrangements for account-based payments for them, so that no eligible beneficiary is deprived of pension benefits due to Aadhaar-related issues.During the presentation, it was informed that Rs 147 crore 5.51 lakh has been allocated in August 2026 for 991,914 beneficiaries under various pension schemes, including old-age, widow, disability, farmer, deserted women, maintenance allowance, Teelu Rauteli and dwarf pension schemes.Of the total pension beneficiaries, 214,711 are covered under the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP), while 777,203 beneficiaries are covered under state-level schemes. Of the pension amount disbursed in August, approximately Rs 140.11 crore constitutes the state's share, while Rs 6.94 crore is the Centre's share.The presentation further stated that a total of 5,605 new pensions were sanctioned under various social security pension schemes in August. These include 3,945 old-age pensions, 1,000 widow pensions, 416 disability pensions, 106 farmer pensions, 23 pensions for deserted women, and 115 beneficiaries under the maintenance allowance scheme.A presentation was also made regarding upcoming programmes. It was informed that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, has proposed a two-day National Departmental Summit on September 18 and 19, 2026, at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre, Janpath, New Delhi. The summit will facilitate dialogue among the Centre, states and Union Territories on key priorities related to social justice and empowerment.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Friday transferred the August 2026 pension instalment under various social security pension schemes of the Social Welfare Department. A total of Rs 147.05 crore was transferred directly into the bank accounts of 991,914 beneficiaries. In August, pensions of 5,605 new beneficiaries were also sanctioned under various pension schemes.

Article Title: ‘Developed countries must take lead': India calls for climate finance after Nepal flood
Article Text:
People walk next to damaged buildings following the deadly flash floods and mudslides in Devighat, Nuwakot district, Nepal (Picture credit: Reuters)

‘ Climate change is a common challenge’

India reiterates support for Nepal

Nepal clarifies compensation remarks

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday said developed countries must take the lead in reducing emissions and support developing nations through finance and technology transfer, reiterating India's position that climate action must be guided by the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.The remarks by MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal came in the aftermath of the devastating flash floods in Nepal and amid questions over remarks concerning climate-related compensation from major economies, including India, China and the United States.Addressing the issue at a weekly media briefing, Jaiswal said India had consistently maintained that climate change was a shared challenge.“I understand that a clarification has also been issued by the Nepalese side. Having said that, let me say that India has consistently maintained that climate change is a common challenge, and action in this regard must be based on the principle of common differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities,” he said.Jaiswal said countries historically responsible for emissions should take the lead in tackling the challenge and supporting developing nations.“Developed countries who historically are responsible for the emissions and have contributed overwhelmingly to the civil crisis, must take lead in reducing emissions and supporting developing countries by way of finance and technology transfer to meet this challenge,” the MEA spokesperson added.Jaiswal also said India had extended solidarity and support to Nepal following the tragedy and would continue to assist the country in its reconstruction and recovery efforts.“In the wake of this tragedy, we have extended our solidarity and support to the government and people of Nepal. As a close friend and partner, India responded promptly, and we will continue to support the reconstruction and recovery efforts in the country,” he said.Referring to Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah's appreciation of India's assistance, Jaiswal said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had spoken to his Nepalese counterpart after the disaster and conveyed India's support.“We have seen that the Prime Minister of Nepal has thanked us for our support... our prime minister spoke to the Prime Minister of Nepal and conveyed that India stands shoulder to shoulder and extends all its support to Nepal in this time of crisis, and it will offer whatever help is required,” he said.Meanwhile, Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal clarified on Thursday that neither he nor the Nepalese government had sought climate-related compensation from India, China or the United States.“Neither I nor anyone in the ministry of foreign affairs or the government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States,” Khanal told news agency ANI.Also read: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floods He said Nepal's appeal was for the global community to recognise climate change and its impact on the country.“Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal,” he added.Khanal also said India, China and Nepal shared environmental ecosystems and should work together to prepare for the impact of climate change in the Himalayas.He stressed the need to look beyond one-time disaster assistance and consider the longer-term effects of rising temperatures and climate change on communities.
Article Summary: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said developed countries must take the lead in reducing emissions and support developing nations through finance and technology transfer. The remarks came in the aftermath of the devastating flash floods in Nepal and amid questions over remarks concerning climate-related compensation from major economies.
